thread:
maya: Kicked off an apples-2-apples run comparing streaming vs non-streaming with the new adaptive batching heuristic. Summary in a sec.
jonah: Nice — which models/hw combo?
maya: Running Llama-2-13B (qat-8) on p4d-like nodes. Matched sequence distributions using replay harness from last week.
priyanka: Important to pin kernel versions too. Are we using the new kernel-selection patch?
maya: Yes, kernel selection v2 enabled (prefer cuattention-v3 for <512 seq, fallback to cuatt-v2 for long). Using same kernel set for both streaming/non-streaming.
kevin: How are you making it apples-2-apples? synthetic traffic can hide KV effects.
maya: Good call. We force-match request ordering and prefix cache state using the replay harness snapshot. Steps:
- replay original client traces (timestamps normalized)
- preload KV cache to observed hit rates
- run streaming and non-streaming with identical arrival times
- collect per-token latency, tail percentiles, kernel choices
sophia: Can you paste the run command? small sanity check.
maya: Sure:
```
./replay-runner --trace=prod-2026-02-12.json --mode=streaming --kernel-policy=v2 --batch-policy=adaptive --preload-kv=kv-snapshot-0212
```
jonah: What does adaptive do now? adjust batch depth or width?
maya: Both. It will grow group size up to 16 tokens or 8 requests depending on latency budget and KV hit signals. It also biases for KV hits to prefer larger batches since those are cheaper.
priyanka: Any perf regressions vs baseline v1?
maya: Short summary: median token latency down ~6% in streaming, p95 down ~12%. Non-streaming median similar, but p99 for non-streaming increased on long seqs by ~9% due to KV churn. Streaming kept p99 stable.
kevin: Do you have a quick table of numbers? even a tiny one inline helps.
maya: inline numbers from 10m sample:
- streaming: med=8.6ms/token, p95=29.4ms, p99=82.1ms
- non-streaming: med=9.1ms/token, p95=33.1ms, p99=89.5ms
jonah: Interesting. Kernel selection differences?
maya: Yes — streaming uses cuattention-v3 ~71% of calls vs non-streaming ~60%. Non-streaming saw more fallback to cuatt-v2 on longer windows because batching collapsed different sequence lengths.
sophia: Backpressure behavior? readloop adjustments?
maya: Observed more readloop stalls in non-streaming when KV cache miss storms happened. We instrumented the client readloop and saw queue growth spikes leading to bigger tail.
priyanka: Can you paste the snippet of the readloop logs where it grows?
maya: paste below (redacted):
```
[readloop] inflight=48 qsize=0 -> inflight=64 qsize=23 (kv-miss-storm)
[readloop] kernel=cuatt-v2 latency=124ms
[readloop] backpressure=true throttle_ms=30
```
kevin: That matches my repro from last month. Might be worth tuning the readloop hysteresis threshold to avoid the 64 -> 80 spike.
jonah: Did you test changing --batch-size hard caps vs adaptive?
maya: Yes. With hard-cap batch-size=8 we saw slightly lower median but worse tails for streaming (less aggregation on KV hits). Adaptive gives better cost/latency balance.
priyanka: Any changes in token cost estimates?
maya: Adaptive reduced GPU token cost by ~4% due to better batch packing and higher KV hit amplification.
infra-bot: deploybot: replay-runner v1.12 completed for job 1851234567; artifacts at s3://rwdn-perf/apples2apples/1851234567/
sophia: Next steps:
- tune readloop hysteresis and throttle backoff
- run longer 4h overnight with varied seq distributions
- try kernel-selection aggressiveness toggle (prefer v3 more)
jonah: Also run an isolated KV miss storm synthetic to validate stability under worst-case.
maya: Agreed. I'll schedule the 4h and synthetic miss-storm. Will post artifacts + plotting script in the run folder. :thumbsup:
kevin: Thanks — helpful and concise. If the overnight looks good we can fold adaptive into default batch policy for streaming.
maya: Will update here once done.
